walkthroughs.body_html: Sea wall at Sea Palling, Norfolk, cost £14 million in 1997. Reflective walls can scour beach. Groynes at Mappleton cost £2 million but caused downdrift erosion at Cowden. Rip-rap is cheaper but visually intrusive.

Beach nourishment at Bournemouth pumped 1.5 million m^3 sand at cost £8 million; widely seen as cost-effective. Dune regeneration at Studland Bay uses marram grass planting. Soft approaches work with natural processes and avoid downdrift damage.

Medmerry (2013) breached sea wall to create 183 hectares of intertidal habitat, protecting 348 homes. Cost £28 million; saved estimated £90 million over 100 years. Created saltmarsh habitat for wildlife and absorbs storm energy.

mcqs.q: Why might managed retreat be more sustainable than building a sea wall?
options: Sea walls are expensive, deflect erosion elsewhere and reflect wave energy worsening beach loss; managed retreat works with natural processes, creates habitat and is cheaper long-term.
Sea walls always solve coastal erosion problems permanently.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.

mcqs.q: What is the ITCZ and why does it bring rain?
options: The Intertropical Convergence Zone is where trade winds from both hemispheres converge near the equator, forcing air to rise, cool and produce heavy convectional rainfall.
Managed retreat means letting all coastal towns disappear into the sea.
The ITCZ is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The ITCZ is a fixed band of permanent storms at the equator.
